title: Ensemble scorer and calibration sink for hybrid quantization validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: build a modular 'ensemble scorer' and a calibration sink to centralize per-profile quality metrics across FP8/INT8 variants and mixed pipelines. The goal is to provide consistent signal for automated calibration, regression detection, and release gating. Scope: implement metric adapters for perplexity (token-level), MMLU-style multi-choice accuracy, Rouge/L(TM)-style for summarization, BLEU for translation, and a pattern for plugging in custom task-specific scorers (QA F1, code exec pass@k). This ticket covers the scorer service, storage schema for per-run snapshots, and the calibration sink that consumes scorer outputs to propose quant thresholds and delta budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Central scorer service accepts standardized payloads and returns metrics for given reference/test pair
Per-profile snapshots stored in the calibration sink with metadata (model, quant profile, seed, prompt-set, ci-run) and are queryable from the console
Adapters implemented for perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, Rouge-L, BLEU, and a plugin hook for task-specific scorers
Calibration sink produces a ranked list of quantization candidate profiles with expected quality delta and confidence intervals
Automated regression alert rule triggers when delta exceeds configured thresholds and posts to the evaluation dashboard and Slack channel
Integration tests cover sampling, seed determinism, and reproduceable metric outputs across FP8/INT8 variants
success_metrics: <2% average MMLU regression vs fp16 baseline on dev prompts for selected profiles
False-positive regression alerts <5% over a 2-week window
End-to-end scoring latency < 200ms per sample for batched jobs (100 samples) on infra-qa
Calibration sink recommendations match human sign-off in 7/10 candidate profiles in initial pilot
implementation_plan: 1) Define scorer API contract (input: request_id, model_version, quant_profile, prompt_id, reference, generation, sampling_seed, metadata). 2) Implement base adapters: perplexity adapter using normalized log-prob sums; MMLU adapter using relaxed answer matching and top-k normalization; Rouge-L using sequence alignment; BLEU with sacreBLEU defaults. 3) Add plugin interface for task scorers (python entrypoints). 4) Calibration sink: ingest scorer outputs, compute delta vs baseline, apply bootstrap resampling to estimate 95% CI, rank profiles by QoE delta and cost delta. 5) Expose results to console via new per-profile dashboard and to runtime via pull API. 6) Add canary pipeline: run on reserved small evaluation set for nightly runs. 7) Document scoring contract and runbooks.
test_plan: - Unit tests for each adapter with edge cases (empty refs, varying tokenization). - Determinism test: fixed seeds produce identical metrics across runs. - Bootstrap CI test: statistical properties validated on synthetic distributions. - End-to-end integration: scoring -> sink -> dashboard -> alert. - Performance: run batched scoring on infra-qa GPU and measure p95 latency. - A/B comparison harness against fp16 baseline with significance testing (paired bootstrap).
design_decisions: Use tokenizer-aligned perplexity (log-prob per token normalized by effective token count) to avoid length bias
MMLU adapter supports both strict-match and relaxed heuristic to handle paraphrases; pilot uses relaxed with manual review threshold
Rouge-L chosen for summarization baseline; we'll add BERTScore later if correlation with human labels is insufficient
Bootstrap resampling (n=1000) selected for CI to avoid parametric assumptions given skewed metric distributions
Store scorer snapshots as compressed NDJSON with hashed prompt-set id to ensure traceability and dedupe
open_questions: Should the calibration sink proactively propose quantization rollback rules vs only flagging candidates?
What is the minimum sample size per task to get stable CI for MMLU-like accuracy? (initial proposal: 500 examples)
Do we want tokenization parity between fp16 baseline and quantized runs or to use model-specific tokenizers?
Where to surface cost delta: token-cost only or end-to-end infra-cost (GPU time + memory)

risks_mitigation: Risk: Metric variance yields noisy recommendations. Mitigation: require min sample size and CI overlap check before proposing profile as safe.
Risk: Tokenization mismatch causes spurious perplexity deltas. Mitigation: enforce shared tokenizer binary and run token-level diff during CI.
Risk: Large scoring cost for heavy tasks. Mitigation: configure adaptive sampling and caching of cached prefix/KV where possible.
